messages:
maria-g: Following the postmortem, we need a concrete runbook update addressing the kv-cache eviction + HPA flapping pattern. Specific ask: triage checklist, quick mitigations, escalation order, and a short test procedure. Who can take which piece?

ethan: I can take the test procedure and a reproducible checklist for dev/staging. plan to write a small harness that simulates high miss rate to validate cache priming.

priya: i'll own alerts + decision thresholds. propose: alert when kv_cache_hit_ratio drops > 12% over 30m AND P50 latency rises > 250ms.

lee: i'll write the escalation sequence and add exact phone/pager steps + what to collect before paging (logs, recent autoscaler events, cache metrics).

jason-w: i'll add the short triage CLI commands and a minimal rollback/fallback command that on-call can run quickly.

oncall-bot: Task created: "inc-runbook: kv-cache + autoscaler playbook updates" assignees: ethan, priya, lee, jason-w. Due: 2026-05-14.

maria-g: good. keep ownership explicit (first.last). Priya, include the decision table for Hosted vs Dedicated customers (who can approve scale overrides).

priya: noted. Draft thresholds and approvers: Hosted -> infra-sre can approve; Dedicated -> product-ops + customer success approval required. will add a tiny decision table in the playbook.

jason-w: triage snippet (to add to runbook):
```bash
# pod health
kubectl get pods -n inference -l app=runtime -o wide
# check runtime metrics
curl -s http://runtime-mgr:9100/metrics | grep -E 'kv_cache_(hit|miss)_ratio'
# recent HPA events
kubectl get events -n inference --field-selector involvedObject.kind=HorizontalPodAutoscaler --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | tail -n 40
# quick mitigation: scale to min replicas 3 (temporary)
kubectl scale hpa inference-runtime --replicas=3 -n inference || kubectl scale deploy/runtime --replicas=3 -n inference
```

lee: escalation snippet i'll add:
"If P95 latency > 1000ms OR errors > 4% for 10m -> page @sre-oncall -> collect `metrics.tar.gz` -> if no ack in 8m -> page infra-lead -> if infra-lead approves -> trigger model-fallback (route 20% to small-pool)"

ethan: for the test harness i'll add a replay job that does cache-miss-heavy loads and a CI job that runs weekly in staging to detect regressions. will include run instructions in the runbook.

priya: alert config draft:
```yaml
- alert: KVCacheHitDrop
  expr: (1 - sum(rate(kv_cache_hit_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_request_total[5m]))) > 0.12
  for: 30m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "KV cache hit ratio drop > 12% over 30m"
```
Add link to dashboard and PagerDuty escalation.

maria-g: automation ask: which mitigations should be auto-remediated? e.g., auto-restart runtime if cache miss rate spikes? or auto-scale override? we must be conservative.

jason-w: propose auto-cache-priming script that runs once on detection (non-blocking), owner = jason-w. Manual approval for override scaling for Dedicated customers.

lee: auto fallback routing should be gated and require a human ack; automation owner = lee. will write playbook steps to validate fallback.

oncall-bot: Reminder: PR requested for runbook edits. Branch: gh/runbook-kv-autoscaler-1812. Reviewers: infra-sre, devex. Due: 2026-05-12.

maria-g: can we have a short QA checklist before merging? include smoke tests: runbook commands execute (without destructive actions), alerts fire in staging, and fallback flips traffic to a canary pool.

ethan: adding QA steps to the PR. also adding a scheduled weekly smoke test job to catch regressions.

priya: i'll wire the alert to a low-severity PagerDuty schedule in staging first, then escalate policy to prod.

jason-w: i'll open the PR tonight: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/pull/448 (WIP)

maria-g: excellent. i'll track these in the postmortem follow-ups sheet and we will review during next incidents sync. please update the sheet with owner, link to PR, and due date.

oncall-bot: Follow-up recorded: [runbook PR #448, alert config patch, test harness job, escalation doc]. Owners: ethan, priya, lee, jason-w. Next check-in: 2026-05-11."
